newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sumatra well stops short of target-Novus.
newsitem.headline: Sumatra well stops short of target-Novus.

text.p: Australia's Novus Petroleum Ltd said on Tuesday the joint venture partners in the Singa-1 exploration well on the Indonesian island of Sumatra had decided to stop drilling short of the well's target depth.
Last month Novus said the well discovered gas at the top of the main reservoir target at 3635 metres.
The target depth for the well was 4115 metres where it was to test a limestone reef known as the Batu Raja formation which hosts oil in the prolific Limau oil trend in South Sumatra.
"The well has not been particularly appropriately engineered to go to these depths," Novus managing director, Bob Williams sold a Securities Institute Association luncheon.
"In the last few days the partners decided the well was not making enough progress, was not cost effective," he said.
Williams said over the next few days the operator would start to test the gas out of the formation.

Australia's Energy Equity Ltd is the operator of the project and has a 20 percent interest. The other partners are Novus with 15 percent, Amerada Hess Corp with 50 percent and Coparex International SA with 15 percent.
Williams said gas flow tests at the top of the reservoir would determine whether or not the discovery was commercial.
He said before the well commenced the partners estimated the prospect could contain up to 1.3 trillion cubic feet of gas.
If this estimate proved correct, Novus' interest in the discovery would equate to 13 million barrels of oil equivalent, he said.
At 3.10 p.m (0510 GMT), Novus shares were two cents weaker at A$4.28 while Energy Equity shares were three cents down at A$1.45.
